issue_context.title: Both flavors of webapi project should use Swashbuckle defaults
issue_context.body:
Right now, the controllers flavor of the webapi project template includes code to configure Swashbuckle (Swagger/OpenAPI) explicitly rather than relying on library defaults. The minimal flavor of the template does not.

Both flavors should be consistent with how they use Swashbuckle, relying on the library defaults and include a comment pointing to our official docs on how to configure it further.

Furthermore, the non-default code we have in the controllers flavor of the template is currently configuring the Swagger UI with a non-relative path, which Swashbuckle itself stopped doing a few versions back as it's known to cause issues with some app deployment configurations (e.g. proxies, forwarders, etc.).

review_comments: please leave in the defaults, as it provides customers guidance on customizing this. Without the parms, there's less guidance when they get started. I know it's more code, but it provides them guidance.

I think there's confusion on the term "defaults" here. When I say "defaults" I mean, call the overload with no arguments and let the framework (Swashbuckle) default all configuration. I'm shooting for the simplest thing that works. Folks should read Swashbuckle documentation to learn how to configure it as it isn't trivial.
How do folks feel about a comment that points to the Swashbuckle docs instead?
I'm okay with no params and a link. I'd love no params, but folks need to be sent to the docs to know how to customize it, for sure.

More on this - the "v1" thing - that has been confusing for a lot of folks as it "looks like" a version, but is used in the original/MVC template as the name of the OpenAPI document. So, this has been a point of confusion, and I've heard from customers during interviews that they get tripped up on it even though they've done it 100 times before. I think no-params-in-the-template could have other consequences, but I'm in agreement with @DamianEdwards that, if we could get it down to no-params, working, and clean, that's the best case.

Defaults from Swashbuckle for the doc appear to come from https://github.com/domaindrivendev/Swashbuckle.AspNetCore/blob/master/src/Swashbuckle.AspNetCore.SwaggerGen/DependencyInjection/ConfigureSwaggerGeneratorOptions.cs#L51

Here's some more detail on the URL specification being absolute vs. relative, seemingly indicating that we really should not be manually setting it in the template to an absolute path as it causes issues https://github.com/domaindrivendev/Swashbuckle.AspNetCore/commit/a2893063ab98a088810c96457a1d61a4a35829e3#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R293
